scenarios.title: A lowercased format lowercases only the tail
scenarios.notes: Risk: lower handling spreads to the prefix or suffix, or to the literal text. Try feature/PROJ-1-{name:lower}, Feat/PROJ-{name:lower}-X, uppercase ids, mixed-case area and profile parts. The literal text keeps its case. {name} keeps the case of the tail. The CLI prints the same branch as the Python name.

scenarios.title: Every kind builds a valid branch that split reverses under three formats
scenarios.notes: Eight kinds times sdlc/{name}, feature/PROJ-1-{name}, feature/PROJ-1-{name:lower}. The branch starts with the prefix, ends with the suffix, and the middle equals the tail (lowercased where asked). Each branch passes git check-ref-format. Try edge parts: area api-v2, state ts, verify round 0 part 0. The parse half joins in S-007, so R-068 stays partial.

scenarios.title: The CLI name agrees with the Python name for all 24 cases
scenarios.notes: Run branches.py name with --format, --kind and parts from a scratch cwd. The branch field equals mod.name. Exit code is 0. A bad kind or format exits non-zero with no stack trace.

scenarios.title: No push or pull-request site names an e2e-area branch
scenarios.notes: Source check over six files. The scan finds at least one real push site, so it cannot pass on an empty match. Try a push that spans more than 4 lines, a push in a comment, and a variable-built branch. Record the limit that the scan names the kind, not the parsed kind.

scenarios.title: A planted e2e-area push is reported by the scanner
scenarios.notes: Run the scanner on git(repo, "push", "-u", "origin", name(fmt, "e2e-area", ...)) and on a pr create line. Each gives a violation. A comment line gives none. Mutation check: the test fails when a scratch copy of state-write.py gets an e2e-area push.

Call name and split in batch over generated parts and formats

riskReason: The slice adds tests only; product code does not change, and a wrong result is easy to see and cheap to fix.
notes: Two profiles cover all five scenarios. The slice row says medium, but no I/O boundary changes and no product code moves. Cap for low is 2 profiles: contract first (covers VS-1, VS-2, VS-4, VS-5), then cli (VS-1, VS-2, VS-3).
